text: Large language models, or LLMs, are artificial intelligence systems trained on massive amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. They learn patterns in language, not facts, by predicting the next word in a sentence over and over. When you type a prompt, the model uses those patterns to generate a likely response. This is why prompt engineering—the skill of asking clear, specific questions—matters so much. A good prompt can produce a useful answer, while a vague one leads to confusion. LLMs can write emails, summarize reports, or explain difficult ideas, but they also have limits. They can invent information, repeat biases from their training data, and struggle with real-time updates. So, treat their output as a helpful starting point, not an absolute truth.
